_about: THE TEST ID INDEX — every test identifier we use, what it asserts, where it runs, and how to run it. Created 2026-08-08 (user) after MAINNETSMOKE-01 and TXS-1 were quoted in chat and could not be found anywhere: they were not tasks, and TXS-* existed only as prose inside QA-XFAIL1.json's `next` field. A test id must resolve to something you can open — that is what this file is for. Viewer: tests.html. Naming convention (PROTOCOL.md): a bare CAPITALISED reference is a kPad TASK; a test id is written T:<id> in prose and chat, and must come with its URL. Each suite records what_it_does (the actual steps), pass_means, fails_when, its dimension and its cost — added 2026-08-08 after the user pointed out that 'real value, real network, once a day' does not tell anyone what the test IS.

convention.task: BARE CAPS — a kPad task, e.g. TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1. Look it up in kPad.
convention.test: T:<id> — a test case, e.g. T:HBARXFER-01. Defined in this file; results on the QA grid.
convention.assertion: T:<suite>.<n> — one assertion inside a suite, e.g. T:A5b.4. Never a task.
convention.reproduction: A FAILING TEST MUST SAY HOW TO REPRODUCE IT. No red is reported — here, in chat, or on the dashboard — without concrete steps someone can follow. If the only way to trigger it is inside a harness, it is a harness artefact and must not be reported as a product failure (WC-RESETWEDGE1, 2026-08-08).

suites.title: The whole thing, end to end
suites.asserts: Two players join a board, one offers HBAR, both lock, the deal strikes, kWallet signs, it settles on Hedera.
suites.notes: Needs a game created on the TARGET's own backend — a board can only play a game its backend knows about, so pointing BASE elsewhere is not sufficient on its own.
what_it_does: Create a fresh public testnet game (own-to-own offers don't work, so every run needs a clean game two real players can join).
Player A opens the board and connects a wallet over WalletConnect — kWallet, our headless test wallet, does the pairing.
Player B opens the SAME board in a separate browser context and joins by typing an account (no wallet — a real second player).
A offers 0.01 HBAR to B via the asset card.
Both players lock. The deal strikes and the signing phase opens.
A taps Sign. kWallet auto-approves. The signature is saved and submitted.
The harness watches A's screen for the verdict toast.
suites.pass_means: A '🟩 Transaction successful' verdict appears on the board and the transfer is real on Hedera testnet. This is the only test that exercises the whole chain — board UI, lock rule, strike, WalletConnect, signing, submission, settlement, verdict.
suites.fails_when: Any link in that chain breaks. Historically its most common failure is harness fragility, not product breakage (see QA-HARNESSREPAIR1).
suites.how_to_reproduce: Run the harness listed above. If it fails, the run log names the failing assertion; the steps under 'What it does' are the manual equivalent.

suites.title: The wallet killed the session and never told us
suites.asserts: You clear connections in HashPack while katomia is CLOSED. Signing must fail fast and honestly instead of hanging. Eight assertions, A5b.1-A5b.8.

assertions.asserts: GHOST successfully created (dApp believes, wallet does not)
sign against a ghost does not hang — must give up inside the tx's validity window, not at the 120s cap
assertions.history: FAILED at exactly 120.0s on lab1 AND production (2026-08-07); the frozen benchmark's only expected_fail. FIXED by TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1 S4 (KWC snapshot 33993b7) — passes on lab1 and pat 2026-08-08. Fixture also corrected to a 40s validity window, matching the board's real one; the SDK default 120s made the <60s assertion unreachable regardless of bundle behaviour.

assertions.asserts: sign against a ghost fails loudly, never silently succeeds
user can re-pair out of the ghost state
sign after re-pair reaches the wallet on the NEW session

what_it_does: Pair with the wallet and establish a real session.
Snapshot the dApp's WalletConnect storage (IndexedDB).
Destroy the session WALLET-SIDE, then restore the snapshot — so the dApp still believes it is connected but the wallet has no record. This is a true 'ghost'.
Attempt to sign against that ghost.
Re-pair and sign again.
suites.pass_means: The ghost sign gives up quickly and loudly, inside the transaction's own validity window — never hangs, never silently 'succeeds'. Then the user can re-pair and sign normally.
suites.fails_when: It hangs (was 120s until TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1 S4), or worse, resolves as if it worked.
suites.why_it_matters: This is the discriminating ghost test — it reproduces the exact scenario where a user clears connections in HashPack while katomia is closed. T:WC-A5-ONLINE passes even on broken bundles; this one does not.
suites.harness_note: lives on the box at /opt/kwallet/ (not web-served — it runs its own in-process wallet peer)
suites.how_to_reproduce: Run the harness listed above. If it fails, the run log names the failing assertion; the steps under 'What it does' are the manual equivalent.

suites.title: The wallet was cleared while katomia was open
suites.asserts: The wallet's delete reaches us, so we should detect it and re-pair cleanly.
suites.state: 8/8 — healthy. Was SILENT for 14 days until 2026-08-08 (an unbounded hang ate the whole run and it reported nothing); harness given step ceilings, and a redundant resetWalletLink removed from its main flow. An A5.0 assertion added the same day was WITHDRAWN hours later: it failed only on accumulated harness state, not on any user path — see WC-RESETWEDGE1 for the full correction.
what_it_does: Pair, and sign once to prove the baseline works.
The USER CLEARS THE CONNECTION IN THEIR WALLET APP while the page is still open (simulated by a real wallet-side disconnect).
Try to sign again WITHOUT reloading and WITHOUT tapping Connect.
Re-pair and sign again.
Separately and last: call resetWalletLink(), reload, and re-initialise (assertion A5.0).
suites.pass_means: Step 3 detects the dead session, refuses to sign against it, and either self-heals onto a live session or reports KWC-GONE — never a silent wrong-session sign, never a hang.
suites.fails_when: The killed session survives in the dApp's storage and gets handed to every later sign (the pre-R2b bug: 'wallet says signed' then a wiped board).
suites.why_it_matters: Note this one passes on pre-fix bundles too, so treat it as a health check rather than proof the ghost handling works.
suites.harness_note: lives on the box at /opt/kwallet/ (not web-served — it runs its own in-process wallet peer)

assertions.asserts: dApp no longer reports a connected account after the wallet-side clear
no sign sent to the dead session
dApp surfaces an actionable error rather than hanging or lying
sign after recovery reaches the wallet on the NEW session

suites.title: The same board flow, on mainnet
suites.asserts: Real value, real network, once a day — the only test here that is not free to run.
suites.state: PASSING again as of 2026-08-08 08:20 (real mainnet transfer, consensus 1786177210.454269104). It was never a product failure: a failed run on 08-07 left its own unanswered pairing proposal in kwallet-mainnet, and the cron's 'skip if any pending item' guard then muted the test entirely — the grid showed '2 consecutive non-passes' when the truth was 'not run since'. Guard now ages pending items (only items <30m old block a run). Two older reds were harness flakes, not product: a #boardPlayerModal pointer-intercept on the lock click (08-06) and the #addAcctJoinAll account-landing race (08-07), both QA-HARNESSREPAIR1.

suites.title: Transaction validity-duration decode matrix
suites.asserts: 12 cases: Long int64 decode, SignedTransaction wrapper, cross-shape misuse fallbacks, absent field, garbage, real production fixture bytes, expiry arithmetic.
suites.reports: stdout only — not on the grid
what_it_does: Feed 12 shapes of transaction bytes to the validity-duration decoders: Long int64, SignedTransaction wrapper, cross-shape misuse, absent field, garbage, real production fixture bytes, and the expiry arithmetic.
suites.pass_means: All 12 decode to the right duration or fall back safely.
suites.fails_when: A decoder silently returns the wrong window — which is how a transaction's real deadline and the UI's idea of it drift apart.
suites.how_to_reproduce: Run the harness listed above. If it fails, the run log names the failing assertion; the steps under 'What it does' are the manual equivalent.

suites.title: Everyone at the table sees the same game
suites.asserts: Three scripted protocol-level clients on a fresh playnet game (joins, add accounts, offers, public + targeted chat, lock toggles): shared state converges identically on every client; per-socket fields (myPlayerId, targeted chat visibility) correctly differ.
suites.schedule: cron, daily 04:10 UTC (statsync-cron.sh) + on demand at every STATSYNC1-affecting change
what_it_does: Create a fresh public playnet game via POST /katomia/create.
Connect clients A, B, C over plain WebSocket (no browser) with distinct playerTokens.
A and B add playnet accounts (alice, bob); C stays a joined-but-accountless watcher.
Cross-offers (apple, banana), one public chat, one TARGETED chat B→A, lock on/off, a reject.
After quiescing, compare each client's final game_state.
suites.pass_means: Shared state (accounts/players/tx) is byte-identical across all three clients; myPlayerId is distinct per socket; the targeted chat reached A and its sender but never C.
suites.fails_when: Any client misses a broadcast, states diverge, or targeted chat leaks — exactly the properties an incremental-update refactor (STATSYNC1) could silently break.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && node statsync-baseline.cjs — assertion lines print pass/fail with detail.

suites.title: What the full-state broadcast costs on the wire
suites.asserts: Message counts, bytes per broadcast, action→broadcast latency for a scripted sequence, plus a 30-chat growth probe showing broadcast size compounding with chat history. Recorded per STATSYNC1 phase; correctness may never regress, bytes must fall by P6.
what_it_does: Same scripted run as T:STATSYNC-01, with every websocket frame measured (bytes, latency).
Then 30 chat messages in a row, recording how each broadcast grows (full chat history rides every broadcast today).
Optionally spectates a live demo game passively (SAMPLE_GAME) for real-traffic sizes.
suites.pass_means: Baseline 2026-08-14: ~1.7-1.9KB/broadcast on a tiny 2-account game, ~2ms latency, growth probe 2071B→6525B over 30 chats (~154B per chat row, compounding). Later phases are judged against this file's benchmarks.
suites.fails_when: A phase re-run shows correctness failures, or (from P3 on) delta-path bytes fail to undercut the full-state baseline.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && SAMPLE_GAME=q-crowd node statsync-baseline.cjs --record — summary JSON printed and written to qa/data/benchmarks/.

suites.title: A delta client sees exactly what a full-state client sees
suites.asserts: A probe client opted into game_delta (wantDelta:true at join) reconstructs state purely by patch application + chatAppend; at every seq its reconstruction is byte-identical to a full-state control client, and deltas undercut full states on the wire.
suites.schedule: cron, daily 04:10 UTC (statsync-cron.sh) + on demand at every STATSYNC1-affecting change
what_it_does: Client D joins with wantDelta:true after three full-state clients; its first broadcast is full, all subsequent are game_delta {seq, baseSeq, patch, chatAppend}.
D applies each patch (kpatch mirror of backend kdiff.js) and appends chat rows by monotonic id, trimming at 150 like the server.
After every broadcast, D's reconstructed shared view is compared against control client C's full game_state at the same seq.
suites.pass_means: One full state then only deltas; reconstruction ≡ control at every overlapping seq; visible chat matches (welcome rows excluded — legitimately per-viewer); delta bytes < full bytes. First green 2026-08-14: 39 deltas, 40/40 seqs identical, 374B vs 3696B avg (~90% saving).
suites.fails_when: Any patch mis-describes a change (reconstruction diverges), chatAppend leaks or drops a row, or a delta is sent to a socket without the right base seq.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && node statsync-baseline.cjs — 02.x assertion lines print pass/fail; a seq mismatch names the exact seq.

suites.title: A client that misses a delta catches up and converges
suites.asserts: A delta client with a simulated lost broadcast detects the seq gap on the next delta, sends game_refresh exactly once (suppressing duplicates while the reply is in flight), receives a targeted full state, and converges with a full-state control client.
suites.schedule: cron, daily 04:10 UTC (statsync-cron.sh) + on demand at every STATSYNC1-affecting change
what_it_does: The delta probe silently drops one incoming game_delta (simulated network loss).
The next delta's baseSeq mismatches its local seq → it sends {type:'game_refresh', gameId} — once, with an in-flight guard, ignoring further deltas meanwhile.
The backend replies with a targeted full game_state (refresh:true) to that socket only and resets its delta base markers.
One more action confirms deltas apply cleanly again and the reconstruction matches control.
suites.pass_means: Exactly one refresh round-trip; no other client receives the refresh reply; post-recovery reconstruction is byte-identical to control. First green 2026-08-14.
suites.fails_when: Gap goes undetected (silent divergence — the worst failure mode of the whole refactor), refresh floods (no in-flight guard), the reply leaks to other sockets, or the client fails to resume deltas after recovery.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && node statsync-baseline.cjs — 03.x assertion lines; DEBUG=1 prints the probe's per-message seq trace.

suites.title: The real board on deltas renders the same game as on full states
suites.asserts: Two headless board pages on one fresh playnet game — one plain, one ?delta=1 — stay state-identical through actions; the delta page provably runs on patches, self-heals a forced seq corruption via game_refresh, and throws zero page errors.
suites.schedule: cron, daily 04:10 UTC (statsync-cron.sh) + before any delta-default promotion
what_it_does: Create a fresh playnet game; a protocol driver client joins and owns two accounts.
Open the board twice headless (Playwright): plain URL and ?delta=1, both with __katomiaTestHooks so __qaGetState exposes state read-only.
Driver performs chats, add-account, an offer, a lock; after each settle the pages' accounts/players/tx and visible chat must match.
Then window.__stateSeq is forcibly corrupted on the delta page; the next broadcast must trigger one game_refresh and full reconvergence.
suites.pass_means: All six assertions green — first green 2026-08-14 (caught a real bug on the way: onmessage declared `const data`, so delta normalisation threw 'Assignment to constant variable' on every delta; states still converged, which is why the zero-page-errors assertion exists).
suites.fails_when: The delta page diverges from the full page, never actually consumes deltas, fails to self-heal a gap, or any page error fires.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && node statsync-frontend.cjs — assertion lines print pass/fail; page errors are dumped verbatim on failure.

suites.title: Admin disclosure — launch-excluded features visible only to admin, clearly badged
what_it_does: From an admin IP (the header.php $katomiaIpAdmin list): assert the disclosed affordances render with the admin-only treatment (body.kadmin, 🛠 admin chip).
From a non-admin vantage (loopback): assert the affordances are absent from the served HTML.
